title: Customer-Facing Hotlines, Help Desks, and Web-Portal Access for Inspection Program Stakeholders
capability_statement:
Parsons delivers an integrated customer and public interface for vehicle inspection programs that combines toll-free motorist hotlines, station/inspector help desks, a web-based portal for authorized stakeholders, and a referee program for complaint resolution. The call center solution is built on Amazon Connect (telephony, ACD, and IVR) integrated with the Zendesk customer relationship management (CRM) platform via Amazon Connect Computer Telephony Integration (CTI), giving customer service representatives an omnichannel workspace that surfaces caller information automatically when an inspection station ID or phone number is passed from the phone system (chunks 1927, 1963, 2182, 2183). Zendesk APIs let Parsons extract data from inspection stations and inspectors to populate "customers" in the CRM, integrate the inspection database and Business Intelligence tools, and support OAuth/token-based authorization with HTTPS Base64-encoded encryption to protect data in transit (chunk 2183).

For help-desk delivery, Parsons partners with subcontractor Dasher Services, Inc., which has more than 15 years operating a call center, more than a decade on a comparable inspection program, and currently handles help-desk support for Commonwealth Medicaid/CHIP programs and data incident response lines from a Harrisburg, Pennsylvania facility (chunks 2178, 2181). The hotlines use existing toll-free numbers, are staffed during the agency's normal business hours (Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. EST), and the customer-service hotline (1-800-265-0921) and station-operator hotline (1-888-265-5909) are publicized in all outreach and communications materials (chunks 2169, 2186, 2188). All calls are recorded and housed on Amazon Connect for quick reference and search; a coded knowledge base in the Call Tracking Application allows agents to retrieve current Program details and tracks the most frequently asked questions, with geographic mapping of call volume and topic to identify communications gaps (chunks 2171, 2187). Agents are trained in Program technical subject matter, obtain inspector certifications, and receive monthly facilitated and corporate training in interpersonal communication, time management, conflict resolution, diversity, and call center delivery, including simulation training for difficult callers (chunks 2186, 2187).

A modernized cloud-hosted web portal application provides authorized agency personnel and inspection-station personnel role-based remote access to the central inspection database. The portal displays station/technician data, audit information, training information, motorist compliance, hearings and suspensions, and a reporting tool with predefined management reports plus ad hoc reporting; access is limited to authorized users identified by the agency, requires username/password, and exposes different functions and features based on assigned role (chunks 2095, 2096). The portal also supports maintenance tasks: adding and deleting technician access numbers and access codes, setting and clearing lockouts, and sending messages to the inspection stations per agency instructions, with mobile-friendly features delivered through new technologies in the AWS cloud environment (chunk 2095). The agency receives unlimited access to all data collected at no per-transaction fee (chunk 2096).

The referee program handles motorist complaints filed through the customer hotline: a hotline representative gathers information and forwards the complaint to the appropriate regional office; a Parsons team member contacts the customer to resolve, and if unresolved, schedules a referee inspection at the original station (or another station if the customer prefers). The referee conducts a station audit, witnesses the inspection using the equipment's referee function, and independently verifies the test result, with documented outcomes forwarded to the agency for action when faulty inspections are identified (chunks 2177, 2178). The customer interface is reinforced by a redundant operations footprint (three regional offices), forwarded telephony for failover, and remote-work-capable staff proven during COVID-19, ensuring station and consumer issues continue to be addressed during emergencies (chunks 2036, 2037).

differentiators:
- **Modern cloud-native call-center stack**: Amazon Connect (ACD, IVR, CTI, call recording) integrated with the Zendesk omnichannel CRM gives agents a single workspace covering phone, email, and web interactions, with auto-populated caller context driven by inspection-station ID or phone number (chunks 1927, 1963, 2182, 2183).
- **Operating help-desk performance well in excess of typical SLAs**: 80% of calls answered in 20 seconds and 100% in under a minute against a four-minute average-wait SLA, with 99.9% phone-system uptime and downtime capped at 0.5% (chunks 2188, 2189).
- **Deep, dedicated call-center subcontractor**: more than 15 years operating a call center, more than 10 years on a comparable I/M program, and current operator of Commonwealth Medicaid/CHIP help desks and data incident response lines from a single in-state Harrisburg facility (chunks 2178, 2181).
- **Agents who are also certified inspectors**: hotline staff obtain state Safety and Emissions Inspector certifications, equipping them to answer technical inspection questions, not just route calls (chunk 2186).
- **Real proven volume**: 36,000+ consumer and 66,000+ station/technician calls fielded in the past five years on a comparable program (chunk 2178).
- **Closed-loop feedback and analytics**: post-interaction CSAT surveys, coded knowledge base for FAQ tracking, and geographic mapping of call volume and topic identify communications gaps and drive continuous improvement (chunks 2171, 2181, 2187).
- **Web portal modernized for AWS cloud and mobile**: role-based, authenticated remote access for agency-authorized users to station/technician, audit, training, motorist compliance, hearings/suspensions, and reporting data, with predefined and ad-hoc reporting and unlimited data access at no per-transaction fee (chunks 2095, 2096).
- **Continuity-tested customer access**: three regional offices, forwarded telephony, and remote-work-capable staff proven during COVID-19 keep the customer hotline and station support reachable during regional emergencies (chunks 2036, 2037).
- **Layered triage that protects agency staff time**: support graduates from customer/station call centers to regional offices to the inspection-database support team and only escalates to the agency when necessary (chunk 2179).
- **Established referee process**: documented intake from the customer hotline, regional triage, scheduled referee inspection, station audit, equipment-referee witness function, and faulty-inspection documentation forwarded to the agency for action (chunks 2177, 2178).
gap_notes:
- **R-048 / R-061 (Access-controlled webpage and Management Console module for Emergency Repair Technician (ERT) repair data entry)**: The evidence describes a modernized AWS-hosted web portal for authorized agency users and inspection-station personnel with role-based access, station/technician maintenance, audit data, and reporting (chunks 2095, 2096), but does NOT specifically describe an ERT-role webpage or a "limited access repair data entry module within the Management Console" for entering repair data. Capture team must either map the existing portal's role-based access to ERT users explicitly or document a new ERT module to be developed.
- **A-014 (Motorist Hotline 98% answer/queue/return-call standard)**: Evidence cites Dasher answering 80% of calls within 20 seconds and 100% within a minute and a 99.9% phone-system uptime (chunk 2188), and confirms the team understands liquidated-damages exposure for missed standards (chunk 2189). The evidence does not specifically cite the "98% of calls received and placed in a call queue, answered within 10 minutes from the queue, or return call within 2 Motorist Hotline Business Hours" standard. The proposal team should either (a) cite the existing 80%/20-second metric as exceeding the 98%/10-minute bar and explicitly commit to the 2-business-hour return-call window, or (b) capture additional past-performance data on the specific metric.
- **A-068 (Take over existing toll-free hotline number on commencement; revert to State on termination)**: Evidence shows Parsons currently maintains and publicizes existing toll-free numbers on a comparable program (chunks 2169, 2186), but does not address transitioning the specific toll-free number into and out of the contractor's control for the target procurement. Capture team should add a transition/turnover statement.
- **A-076 (Hire and train all Call Center Representatives)**: Evidence describes Dasher's training program (interpersonal communication, time management, conflict resolution, diversity, simulation training, monthly sessions, inspector certification) and confirms the partner is a hire-and-train-capable in-state SDB call-center operator (chunks 2186, 2187). The evidence supports the requirement; no gap identified beyond a direct commitment statement.
- **A-017 (Advance written agency approval for any motorist appointment system) and A-018 (Reservation system accessible via website and telephone)**: The evidence does NOT describe a motorist appointment/reservation system. Existing customer touchpoints described are the toll-free hotline, web portal, referee scheduling, and Zendesk CRM workspace (chunks 2095, 2096, 2177, 2182, 2183). If a reservation system is required for this procurement, capture team must source a separate solution description; the current Parsons evidence cannot substantiate this requirement.
- **General**: All cited customer-interface technology (Amazon Connect, Zendesk, AWS-hosted web portal) is described in proposal voice rather than with delivered, post-implementation performance data on the specific tooling on the Commonwealth program; capture team should pull post-implementation metrics (deflection rates, CSAT scores, ticket close times) where available to convert claims into measured outcomes.
